quotes.text: We'll work with you to determine your eligibility and add you to the waitlist if you qualify.
Customers can initiate a dispute within 120 calendar days of the transaction.
You must submit the requested information within 15 calendar days.
When a refund succeeds, the [Refund](https://docs.stripe.com/api/refunds/object.md) object’s status transitions to `succeeded`.

old_evidence.text: You must submit the requested information within 12 calendar days.
The maximum charge limit is 19,999,99 EUR or the equivalent for other supported currencies.

findings: Both captures describe a B2B 30-day net invoice offer with customer-initiated Mondu redirect for a credit check and merchant return, and label payout timing Standard. The phrase ‘paid upfront’/‘paid immediately’ concerns the offer language and does not establish bank payout on any particular schedule, order completion, or successful individual credit adjudication or payment (old raw lines 6–34; new raw lines 7–35).

The separate lists give EU/UK customer coverage, 14 Stripe-account business locations (AT, BE, CH, DE, DK, ES, FI, FR, GB, IT, NL, NO, PL, SE) and EUR, CHF, GBP presentment. The unchanged currency map gives EUR default and EUR for the specified 13 countries, CHF for CH, GBP for GB. The method-level map does not prove every currency works through Checkout, and CH in the business list does not broaden the separately labeled customer locations (old lines 12–18, 52–69, 255–261; new lines 13–19, 53–70, 267–273).

November still lists Payment Links, Checkout and Elements (Checkout setup and subscription modes excluded; Express Checkout Element unsupported), customer-initiated confirmation, no recurring payments, manual capture support and full/partial refunds (new lines 21–51, 72–80). Stripe Dashboard enablement/dynamic presentation and the manual configuration route remain (old 86–99, new 98–111). November adds a conditional early-access waitlist; being in a supported country, submitting an email, or finding a supported product entry does not establish merchant or Connect activation.

Customer filing deadline newly stated as 120 calendar days from the transaction; merchant evidence text changes 12 to 15 calendar days. The latter is an evidence-submission deadline, and the guide does not state its start trigger. Stripe notifies by email, Dashboard or configured webhook (`charge.dispute.created`), holds the disputed amount pending Mondu resolution, and returns it to Stripe balance if the merchant wins; otherwise the disputed amount stays with the customer. Dashboard and API evidence routes remain (old lines 222–244; new lines 234–256).

Both versions support full and partial refunds up to 180 days after purchase with asynchronous completion described as up to five minutes. Final outcome arrives via `refund.updated` or `refund.failed`; `Refund.status=succeeded` is success, and if failed the amount returns to Stripe balance and the merchant must arrange an alternate refund (old lines 246–253; new lines 258–265). Refund creation and webhook names alone do not prove bank transfer or customer receipt.

The full prohibited-list block is identical at old lines 109–220 and new lines 121–232, with 112 bullet lines including near-duplicates and Mondu's discretionary catch-all. Current source lines 13 and 25 say ‘~90’ and claim the most extensive list; that count does not match the displayed entries and the provider page cannot rank methods. Source line 19's 19,999.99 EUR cap is supported by November and its currency equivalent wording, while May shows a malformed delimiter. Neither document supplies a minimum.

Root index line 7 → Stripe index lines 341–342 and 747 → Stripe BNPL concept lines 22, 32–34, 180–192 and 262–263. Reconcile Mondu's dated Connect and dispute claims there and in the BNPL overview’s conflict discussion, retaining its separate comparisons for other methods. The current method summary only links the May capture.

The separate BNPL overview tables already marked Mondu Connect Supported in May and still do in November (related May overview lines 40–48 and November overview lines 41–49). It is a change in the method page and alignment with the November table, without account-level or supported charge-type details.

This is a newly documented onboarding route alongside unchanged Dashboard enablement, without proving mandatory waitlisting for every account, rollout timing, or successful provisioning.

November adds a customer dispute-filing limit of 120 calendar days from the transaction and changes the time given for merchant evidence from 12 to 15 calendar days (old raw 222–244; new raw 234–256; diff 74–88). Keep filing and evidence deadlines distinct.
historical_claims_to_preserve: The May 6, 2026 method-specific Connect No and 12-calendar-day evidence wording remain dated historical claims. May did not state a customer filing window. November Yes and 15 days supersede those cells in the newer method capture and add the 120-calendar-day filing statement.

The same 30-day invoice, credit-check redirect/return and Standard payout wording, separately scoped presentment and business/customer locations, no recurring payments, no ECE, no Checkout subscription/setup modes, manual capture and stateful refunds persist across the two dates (old lines 6–79 and 246–261, new 7–80 and 258–273).

Presentation changes include adding variant/mode hyperlinks in product support, an updated Elements quickstart URL, whitespace/headers, and correction of old `19,999,99` punctuation to `19,999.99` (old lines 71–103; new lines 72–115). The product methods, video, cap as read in November, prohibited bullet block, and currency mapping do not establish new capabilities from formatting.
conflicts: Current source lines 13/17 and concept 182/262 give ‘no Connect’, while new method properties are Yes (new lines 37–39). Source line 21 and concept line 186 give older 12-calendar-day evidence clock rather than November 15 and omit the distinct new 120-calendar-day filing clock. Reciprocal Stripe BNPL concept line 34 and BNPL overview source line 21 should distinguish the historic May Mondu conflict (May method No vs May cross-method Supported) from November’s matching Yes/Supported, without collapsing unrelated method conflicts or implying Connect eligibility/charge type.

Cross-method tables give Mondu PaymentIntents, manual capture, redirect and footnoted `setup_future_usage` support, but no SetupIntents or billing Subscriptions. The general off_session-only footnote for other supported methods does not turn a setup parameter into recurring authorization; the method page says recurring payments No. The cross-method November Mobile Payment Element cell changes from May Unsupported to Supported, whereas the method page and acceptance index do not expose a mobile integration route. Keep the independently dated product cell separate from the method-specific guide’s Checkout, Elements and Direct API routes (both BNPL overview tables 38–72; related new acceptance lines 9–17).

External ‘paid immediately’ offer and Standard payout property coexist in both captures, without proof of merchant bank funds availability or credit-check approval. Likewise preserve the May full acceptance guide’s historic EUR Checkout and Checkout Sessions compatibility, distinct from the method-level currencies and Direct API country map (acceptance old lines 18–35, 95–112 and 1376–1380). November acceptance parent provides navigation only. Optional seven-day manual PaymentIntent capture remains scoped to the dated detailed acceptance flow, not guaranteed by the overview’s Yes (old acceptance lines 1094–1103, 1122–1139).

Current source lines 13 and 25 exaggerate the listing's size/rank. The same 112 displayed bullet lines (including near-duplicate categories and a discretionary catch-all) are not a verified set of 112 distinct restrictions or a cross-method ranking.
unresolved_questions: The exact eligible Connect account and charge configurations, early access availability for a particular account, selected buyer approval, timing of bank payout, and evidence-clock trigger are not established by these captures. November linked acceptance variants and any mobile implementation were not read.

findings: Add the November full overview and date May provenance. Update supported Connect label with early-access/eligibility qualification, the distinct dispute filing and evidence deadlines, and the refund/Stripe-balance outcomes. Keep scheme/product, method-level currencies and UI-specific scope separate (new raw lines 7–92, 234–273).

Replace the unsupported prohibited-category count and rank at lines 13 and 25 with the unchanged eligibility list locator and discretionary caveat. If stating no minimum, frame it as a detail not supplied by either capture.
conflicts: Source lines 13 and 17 say no Connect, and line 21 treats the May 12-calendar-day evidence deadline as current. New lines 37–39 and 234–256 change those readings. Apply the same dated distinction in the BNPL concept and cross-method source, separately from recurring/no SetupIntents, mobile matrix, acceptance index and the immediate-vs-Standard payout wording.
source_assessments.reason: A reader could incorrectly rule out a Mondu Connect path or compute the wrong filing or evidence deadline from the current answer. The source only routes to old raw, where the newer evidence is unavailable. A dated reciprocal route keeps authorisation, payout, availability and refund states scoped.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mondu, the November 7, 2026 guide describes B2B invoices on 30-day net terms and a customer-initiated redirect to Mondu for a credit check, followed by return to the merchant. Both captures list EU/UK customers, 14 Stripe-account business locations, EUR/CHF/GBP presentment by country with EUR default, and Standard payout timing. The paid-upfront wording does not prove bank payout, and browser return does not prove approval or payment success (old raw lines 6-79, new raw lines 7-80, old raw lines 255-261 and new raw lines 267-273). The method lists Payment Links, Checkout and Elements, with no Express Checkout Element, no Checkout setup or subscription modes, and no recurring payments. It documents manual capture support and a maximum of 19,999.99 EUR or equivalent (new raw lines 41-51 and new raw lines 113-115). Dashboard enablement and dynamic selection remain, and November adds an email-based early access eligibility review and conditional waitlist alongside the method’s Connect Yes (old raw lines 36-38 and old raw lines 86-99, new raw lines 37-39 and new raw lines 72-111). November gives customers 120 calendar days from the transaction to dispute and merchants 15 calendar days to submit evidence. Stripe can notify through email, Dashboard, or the configured `charge.dispute.created` webhook and holds the disputed amount pending Mondu’s decision. A merchant win returns it to the Stripe balance. A customer win leaves it with the customer. Full and partial refunds up to 180 days after purchase remain asynchronous, up to five minutes, with final `Refund` state and `refund.updated` or `refund.failed` events. Failed refunds return the amount to the Stripe balance and require an alternative merchant refund (old raw lines 222-253, new raw lines 234-265). `source-stripe-mondu.md` retains May No and 12-day evidence wording and needs the dated changes and state qualifications.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mondu, the substantive November changes are method-level Connect No to Yes, new eligibility screening and conditional early-access waitlist, added customer filing limit of 120 calendar days from the transaction, and merchant evidence deadline 12 to 15 calendar days (old raw lines 36-38, new raw lines 37-39 and new raw lines 82-92, old raw lines 222-244 and new raw lines 234-256). The guide does not specify a start for counting the evidence period. Keep May No and 12 days dated in `source-stripe-mondu.md`, the Stripe BNPL concept and the separate overview route. The cross-method tables already marked Connect Supported in May and do in November. November’s method Yes aligns with that capture without specifying account eligibility or charge types. Do not confuse the cross-method footnoted `setup_future_usage` flag with recurring payments, or use its Mobile Payment Element cell as an implementation from the acceptance parent. New Checkout and Elements links, the quickstart path, punctuation in the 19,999.99 EUR maximum, and formatting are presentational or navigational. The prohibited bullet block is unchanged and does not establish a cross-method ranking (old raw lines 71-107 and old raw lines 109-220, new raw lines 72-119 and new raw lines 121-232). Preserve the May detailed EUR-only Checkout compatibility separately from the overview’s currency map, the optional manual PaymentIntent capture schedule as acceptance-guide evidence, and the specific distinction between instant merchant-offer language, Standard payout and actual bank availability (old raw lines 6-38 and old raw lines 255-261, new raw lines 7-39 and new raw lines 267-273).
